purpose: Repair the two occurrences of the vacuous UTF-8/scalar ordering caveat carried by v1. Nothing else changes.
whyASuccessorAndNotAnEdit: v1 is hard-pinned BY DIGEST in ten artifacts (plan-and-policy-identity-recipes.v2, execution-plan-commitment.investigation.v1, code-only-identity-rules.sweep.v1, evidence-identity-recipes.v3/v4/v5, evidence-identity-recipes.v3/v5 reviews, r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.7 and its review, plus the freeze payload manifest). Editing v1 in place would silently falsify all ten. Freeze §7.2 and §7.6: repairs are successors.

theMeasurement.method: Exhaustive, not sampled. Every valid Unicode scalar 0x0000-0x10FFFF excluding surrogates D800-DFFF.
theMeasurement.stringLevelCheck: 18102 distinct strings drawn from a pool spanning 1-, 2-, 3- and 4-byte scalars: UTF-8 sort == code-point sort TRUE; UTF-16 sort == code-point sort FALSE, first divergence at index 22.
theMeasurement.conclusion: UTF-8 byte order IS Unicode scalar-value order. v1's caveat named two spellings of one order and called them different.

whyThisMattered: The false half was the JUSTIFICATION of a disclosed limitation, so it read as candour and four independent reviews passed over it. Because the two named policies are one policy, the caveat disclosed nothing -- and it displaced the real undetermined pair, {scalar == UTF-8} vs {UTF-16 code units}, which is live as canonical-json-profile.v1 UR-1 and reaches applied delivery.v4, whose release-manifest canonicalisation is defined as sha256 over JCS -- and RFC 8785 JCS sorts by UTF-16 code units.

derivedFrom.rule: apply operations in order; every set carries its exact prior value

operations.value: INCOMPLETE. The chain reaches a definition, but two gaps remain and the corpus names both: no artifact ever STATES that this field uses canonicalJsonRawCas (it is inferred from the RawCasRef<...> type), and the one reproduction was over a pure-ASCII bundle, so it cannot distinguish escaping policies for non-ASCII, nor key-sort by Unicode scalar value from key-sort by UTF-16 code units. CORRECTED v2: scalar-value order and UTF-8-byte order are the SAME total order -- measured exhaustively over all 1112064 valid scalars, zero inversions -- so v1's stated pair was vacuous. The pair that genuinely diverges is {scalar == UTF-8} versus {UTF-16 code units, as RFC 8785 JCS specifies}, first differing at U+FFFF vs U+10000; see canonical-json-profile.v1#$.undeterminedRegister.UR-1, which remains OPEN.
operations.why: vacuous caveat: scalar and UTF-8 orders are identical; name the pair that actually diverges

operations.from: evaluationProofBundleCasRef -- the single reproduction was over a pure-ASCII bundle and cannot distinguish key-sort by Unicode scalar value from key-sort by UTF-8 bytes, which differ above the BMP.
operations.value: evaluationProofBundleCasRef -- the single reproduction was over a pure-ASCII bundle and cannot distinguish key-sort by Unicode scalar value from key-sort by UTF-16 code units. CORRECTED v2: scalar-value order == UTF-8-byte order (exhaustively measured, 0 inversions over 1112064 scalars); v1 named a pair that cannot differ. The live divergence is against JCS-style UTF-16 ordering, settled by keys U+E000 and U+10000: scalar/UTF-8 emit U+E000 first, UTF-16 emits U+10000 first because its surrogate pair opens 0xD800 < 0xE000.
